summary: D. Max Moerman works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a post at Barnard College (attested 2007–2008) and is attested in 2026 as Professor and Department Chair at Barnard College, Columbia University.

D. N. Shukla was an Indologist who earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer. He held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

D. Neil Schmid works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.

D. Phillip Stanley, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

Dagfinn Føllesdal (1932–2026) was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under W. V. O. Quine. He held professorships at the University of Oslo (~1967–1999) and Stanford University (1968–2011).
Dagmar Schwerk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg (~2008–2017) and was appointed professor at the University of Leipzig around 2023.

Daichi Tado is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. Attested in 2026, he has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Daiei Kaneko (1881–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1901–1904) and under Manshi Kiyozawa, later holding faculty posts at Otani University (~1911–1951) and Toyo University (~1916–1928).
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied and held a post as a research student (研究生) at Ryukoku University (attested 2006).

Daijaku Judith Kinst is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She served as a faculty member at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Daijo Tokiwa (1870–1945) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, he served there as lecturer (1907) and professor (1925–1931), and as professor at Toyo University (1931).

Daiki Sasaki (born 1977) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1996–2005), where he later taught as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015) and faculty member (~2020), and was a full-time lecturer at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji under Eko Hashimoto and Daicho Hayashi. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission and as interim abbot of San Francisco Zen Center (1984–1985).

Dairyu Michael Wenger (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. at The New School, studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman, served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–2012), and guided Dragons Leap Meditation Center (~2012).

D. T. Suzuki (1870–1966) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Soyen Shaku. He held professorships at Otani University (1921–1960) and Columbia University (1952–1957), also teaching at Gakushuin and Tokyo.

Daishun Ueyama (1934–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as associate professor (~1970–1977), professor (~1977–2003), and university president (~1999–2003).

Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku and Otani Universities, and taught at Toyo University (~1907–1927), the University of Tokyo (1923), Komazawa University, and Rissho University.

Daiun Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University (~1898–1901) under teachers including Sotan Oka and Dokutan Sōsan. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (1911–1923).

Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, W. Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and served as a professor of religious studies and Asian studies at Occidental College (~1980–2017).

Dalsukh Malvania (1910–2000) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1959), as Director of the L. D. Institute of Indology (~1963–1977), and held posts at the University of Toronto and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.
